title: Mountain View
name: Mountain View
metaTitle: 1031 Exchange Advisory in Mountain View, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange advisory for Mountain View investors weighing North Bayshore single-tenant campus product against the smaller multi-tenant pool available downtown.

sections.html: Mountain View's commercial identity is shaped almost entirely by North Bayshore, where large single-tenant campus buildings constructed for one dominant technology employer make up most of the square footage in that part of the city. An exchange buyer here needs to understand upfront just how narrow the multi-tenant replacement pool actually is compared to almost anywhere else on the Peninsula.

sections.heading: A Market Concentrated Around One Employer's Real Estate Footprint
sections.html:
North Bayshore has developed almost entirely around a single dominant technology employer's expanding campus footprint, and the buildings there were largely built to that company's specifications rather than as speculative multi-tenant product. That leaves relatively little available inventory for an outside investor to actually acquire, since most of what exists is either owner-occupied or leased under long-term single-tenant arrangements that rarely trade on the open market at all.

Downtown Mountain View along Castro Street offers a smaller-scale alternative, with retail and small office space serving local and regional tenants rather than the technology-campus tenant base found near the bay.

sections.heading: What A Facilities Manager Sees Differently on a Single-Tenant Campus
sections.html:
A facilities manager running a single-tenant North Bayshore building deals with a fundamentally different set of daily concerns than a multi-tenant property manager, since there is no shared common area billing, no competing tenant improvement schedules, and typically direct coordination with one occupant's internal facilities team rather than a leasing office. We ask engineering contacts on any single-tenant candidate to confirm:

  • whether building systems were customized to the current tenant's specific operational needs
  • remaining useful life on HVAC and electrical infrastructure built to that tenant's original specification
  • data center or server room cooling capacity where applicable
  • parking ratio adequacy for the tenant's current headcount
  • site access and security infrastructure tied to that tenant's protocols

sections.heading: Concentration Risk Is the Central Underwriting Question
sections.html:
The biggest risk in a Mountain View single-tenant campus purchase is not mechanical condition but tenant concentration, since one lease decision determines the entire building's income. A buyer should model what re-leasing or repositioning would cost if that tenant vacated, including how much of the building's current infrastructure was built specifically for that occupant's use and would need to be reconfigured for a different type of tenant.

Downtown Castro Street product carries the opposite profile, spreading risk across more, smaller tenants but offering less income certainty from any single lease, which is a tradeoff worth weighing directly against an investor's tolerance for concentration risk rather than assuming one structure is universally safer than the other.

sections.heading: Tenant Coordination Looks Nothing Like a Typical Office Building
sections.html: Because so much of North Bayshore is single-tenant, day-to-day tenant coordination for a facilities manager there often means working directly with the occupant's own internal real estate and facilities staff rather than juggling multiple lease schedules. Downtime, in the traditional sense of vacant space between tenants, is largely irrelevant to this category since these buildings rarely sit empty, but that also means an owner has essentially no diversification if the single tenant's needs change, a tradeoff worth naming plainly rather than glossing over during identification.

sections.heading: Underwriting the Narrow Mountain View Replacement Pool
sections.html:
Because so little multi-tenant product exists in Mountain View, an exchange buyer under 45-day pressure should expect to widen the search to neighboring Sunnyvale or Palo Alto candidates as backups rather than assume enough comparable Mountain View inventory will surface in time. Any single-tenant candidate should be underwritten with a real re-leasing capital estimate built in, not treated as a stabilized asset requiring no future investment.

A facilities manager who has worked inside one of these North Bayshore buildings can usually give a far more grounded read on what a reconfiguration would actually cost than a broker's opinion of value, since that person knows which systems were customized for the current occupant and which are closer to standard office equipment. An exchange buyer should treat that conversation as part of core underwriting rather than an optional extra, given how much of a single-tenant building's future value depends on how expensive it would be to repurpose for a different kind of tenant.

faqs.q: Why is there so little multi-tenant office space available in Mountain View?
faqs.a: North Bayshore developed almost entirely around one dominant technology employer's expanding campus, and most of that square footage is either owner-occupied or leased under long-term single-tenant arrangements that rarely come to market.

faqs.q: What is the biggest risk in buying a single-tenant Mountain View campus building?
faqs.a: Tenant concentration. One lease decision determines the entire building's income, so a buyer should model the cost of re-leasing or reconfiguring the building if that tenant vacated.

faqs.q: How is facilities management different on a single-tenant campus versus a multi-tenant building?
faqs.a: Coordination usually runs directly with the tenant's own internal facilities team rather than across multiple lease schedules, and traditional vacancy downtime is largely irrelevant since these buildings rarely sit empty.

faqs.q: Should I widen my search beyond Mountain View if I cannot find a replacement candidate in time?
faqs.a: Given how narrow the local multi-tenant pool is, many investors keep Sunnyvale or Palo Alto candidates on the identification list as backups from the start rather than waiting to see if a Mountain View option appears.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange San Francisco confirm my Mountain View property qualifies for exchange treatment?
faqs.a: No. We coordinate planning, property identification, and communication among an investor's advisors. Qualification is determined by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.
